items.claim: The theophany onset at Isa.30.27 and the Topheth-image close at Isa.30.33 are independently marked and rightly held apart from the preceding promise oracle.
items.evidence: The opening Hebrew clause (byte tier) and the closing WEB clause both check out verbatim against source; a setumah mark is confirmed at both the front seam (Isa.30.26) and the row's own close (Isa.30.33), with no other span-relevant parashah mark between them, so disclosure is complete on both sides. The strongest real rival -- merging this theophany into the preceding restoration oracle, since neither seam carries a hoy, massa, or koh-amar marker of its own -- is the one actually named, not a strawman. The span (seven of chapter 30's thirty-three verses) is neither a whole-chapter span nor a listed hazard zone, so the high confidence is not miscalibrated.
tier_citations: byte (Hebrew and WEB quotes verified verbatim against source)
tier-3 single-witness (setumah at Isa.30.26 and Isa.30.33)

items.claim: This row's span is the whole of chapter 31 (all nine verses), and its medium confidence sits one band above the ceiling the campaign holds for any whole-chapter span.
items.evidence: Cross-checked against two independent staged inventories, WEB Isaiah 31 has exactly nine verses, and this row's span (31:1-31:9) is the complete chapter -- a maximal unit regardless of how clearly its onset is marked. The hoy onset, the qadosh-Israel title inside it, the divine-frame formula at 31:4, and both setumah marks (31:3, 31:9) are all accurately disclosed and byte-verified, and the paseq at 31:4 is correctly tallied as presence-only; the seam warrant itself is sound. The defect is confidence calibration alone: a chapter-length span should not sit above medium_low.
tier_citations: verse-count cross-check (two independent inventories agree: nine verses)

items.claim: The topic onset at Isa.32.1 and the vocative onset opening the following unit at Isa.32.9 correctly bracket this row, and its topic-onset boundary basis is properly disclosed as a deviation from the hoy/massa default.
items.evidence: WEB quotes at 32:1, 32:8, and the preview of 32:9 check out verbatim; the petuchah at the row's own close (32:8) and the setumah just ahead of its onset (31:9) are both confirmed, and no other span-relevant parashah mark falls inside 32:1-32:8 (a ketiv/qere note at 32:7 is not engaged by any counting or slicing claim here, so no symmetry gap arises). The rejected alternative (a split at 32:5) is a genuine, correctly-declined rival since no addressee or frame shift occurs there. The span is eight of chapter 32's twenty verses, not a whole-chapter span, so high confidence is not miscalibrated.

items.claim: The vocative onset at Isa.32.9 and the syntactic continuity binding Isa.32.14 to Isa.32.15 into a single WEB sentence are both independently verifiable and correctly keep this row from cutting at that verse boundary.
items.evidence: Direct comparison against the folded WEB text confirms 32:14 ends on an open comma ('...a pasture of flocks,') and 32:15 continues lower-case with 'until...', closing the sentence with a period -- a genuine cross-verse syntactic unit correctly held together rather than split. The petuchah ahead of the row's onset (32:8) and the ketiv/qere note inside the row's own span (32:15) are both accurately disclosed without adjudicating the reading. All WEB quotes verified verbatim; confidence medium_low is reasonable given the disclosed construal question over the embedded Spirit-outpouring clause, and the span is not whole-chapter.

items.claim: The register shift from direct address to third-person description at Isa.32.16 and the setumah at the row's own close (32:20) are correctly disclosed as this row's operative-category boundary basis.
items.evidence: WEB quotes at 32:16 and 32:20 check out verbatim; the setumah at 32:20 is confirmed and no other span-relevant parashah mark falls inside 32:16-32:20. items.claim: This whole-chapter hoy-framed complex correctly holds its internal speech-acts under the chapter's own hoy onset, reports the medium_low confidence its whole-chapter span requires, and names the strongest real rival rather than a strawman.
items.evidence: The hoy onset at 33:1 is verified as the sixth of exactly six hoy onsets across chapters 28-33. All three interior setumah marks (33:1, 33:6, 33:12), the setumah just ahead of the onset (32:20), and the paseq at 33:14 are present and fully disclosed with no span-relevant parashah mark omitted. Confidence medium_low sits exactly at, not above, the campaign's whole-chapter ceiling.

items.claim: This row's span is the whole of chapter 35 (all ten verses) at high confidence, two bands above the campaign's whole-chapter ceiling, and its own closing WEB quotation of Isa.35.10 inserts a stray quotation mark not present in the source.
items.evidence: Cross-checked against two independent staged inventories, WEB Isaiah 35 has exactly ten verses, and this row's span (35:1-35:10) is the complete chapter, so confidence should not exceed medium_low regardless of how clearly the onset and close are marked. Separately, a character-level comparison of the row's quoted closing clause against the folded WEB text shows the source ends with a single closing curly quotation mark (the passage is one continuous quoted speech running from 35:4), while the row's own quotation of that same clause inserts a straight double-quote immediately before that curly mark -- an extra character absent from the source, breaking verbatim fidelity on the row's own boundary-closing citation. Neither defect changes the underlying seam determination: the petuchah at 35:10 and the mandatory frame seam at 35:10|36:1 both independently support this row's close.
tier_citations: tier-3 single-witness (setumah at 34:17 and 35:2, petuchah at 35:10)
verse-count cross-check (two independent inventories agree: ten verses)
